sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Langflow is a visual builder for AI agents and workflows. You connect blocks for models, prompts, tools and data on a canvas, test them in a playground, and then serve the result as an API or an MCP tool.
sixtySeconds.problem: Wiring together language models, vector databases and tools in code takes time and is hard to iterate on. Langflow lets you build and test those flows visually while still being able to edit any component in Python.
whoFor: Developers prototyping AI agents and RAG apps quickly
Teams that want a visual way to build and share AI workflows
Builders who want to expose a workflow as an API or MCP server
Python developers who want to customize components
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want a visual canvas with real code underneath and built-in API and MCP serving. If you prefer to write everything in code, a plain Python framework may suit you better.
requirements: Or: Docker, or Langflow Desktop for Windows and macOS
API keys for whichever model providers you connect

overview: Langflow gives you a canvas where each block is a component: a language model, a prompt, a vector store, a tool or an agent. You connect them into a flow and run it step by step in the interactive playground to see what each part does.

Every flow can be deployed as an API, exported as JSON for use in Python apps, or turned into an MCP server so other AI tools can call it. The README says it supports all major LLMs and vector databases, multi-agent orchestration, and observability through LangSmith, LangFuse and other integrations.

There are three ways to run it: Langflow Desktop for Windows and macOS with everything bundled, the Python package installed with uv, or the official Docker image. Release packages and Docker images require you to set an administrator password before starting.

install.verificationNote: Commands come from Langflow's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

steps.title: Set an administrator password
steps.body: Release packages disable automatic login. Set LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD, then sign in as langflow.
steps.code:
read -rsp "Langflow administrator password: " LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD; echo
export LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD

steps.title: Set a password and start the container
steps.body: Official Docker images require authentication. Sign in as langflow with the password you entered.
steps.code:
read -rsp "Langflow administrator password: " LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD; echo
export LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD
docker run -p 7860:7860 -e LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD langflowai/langflow:latest

steps.title: Download Langflow Desktop
steps.body: Available for Windows and macOS with all dependencies included, so there's no Python setup. Download it from langflow.org/desktop.

environment.name: LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD

troubleshooting.problem: Langflow asks for a login you never set
troubleshooting.solution: Release packages and Docker images disable automatic login. Set LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD before starting and sign in as langflow.

troubleshooting.problem: Install fails on your Python version
troubleshooting.solution: Langflow needs Python 3.10 to 3.14. Check your version and use uv, which the README recommends.

troubleshooting.problem: Upgrading from an older auto-login install
troubleshooting.solution: Follow the upgrade instructions in Langflow's authentication docs before switching defaults.
